hero.headline: House votes to limit Trump's war powers on Iran in bipartisan rebuke
hero.body:
The House of Representatives passed a war powers resolution on Wednesday directing President Trump to end military hostilities with Iran, marking a rare bipartisan rebuke of the administration's military actions. The vote passed 215-208, with four Republicans joining Democrats to support the measure after it had failed in three previous attempts.

The Republican lawmakers who crossed party lines were Thomas Massie of Kentucky, Brian Fitzpatrick of Pennsylvania, Warren Davidson of Ohio and Tom Barrett of Michigan. The vote represents growing erosion of Republican support for the conflict as it continues without clear congressional authorization.

"The House should use this moment to do what we should have done before the war started—discuss the rationale, strategy, end state, and costs to American taxpayers and our economy," said Senator Tim Kaine, who sponsored the Senate version of the bill, in a statement before the vote.

The resolution comes as military tensions between the United States and Iran continue to escalate. Iranian drone strikes on Kuwait's airport resulted in casualties, with Iran describing the attack as retaliation for earlier US strikes on an Iranian oil tanker and island. The back-and-forth military actions have raised concerns about a broader regional conflict.

Despite the House vote, the measure faces significant obstacles. Democrats have been unable to advance a similar war powers resolution in the Senate, where Republicans hold control. Even if both chambers were to pass the resolution, Trump would likely veto it. Congress would need a two-thirds majority in both the House and Senate to override a presidential veto, which remains unlikely given current party divisions.

The Senate previously voted to advance its own war powers resolution in a 50-47 vote, marking the first time the chamber had advanced the bill since the conflict began in February. Four Republicans joined Democrats in supporting the procedural vote, including Senator Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, who cited lack of clarity from the administration about military objectives.

The bipartisan nature of the votes reflects growing concern among lawmakers about the administration's military approach to Iran. Both Republican and Democratic critics have argued that the president lacks proper congressional authorization for sustained military operations. The resolution does not require immediate withdrawal but seeks to prevent further escalation without congressional approval.

The war powers debate revives longstanding tensions between the executive and legislative branches over who holds authority to commit US forces to combat. Senate Democratic leaders pointed to the votes as evidence of growing pressure on Republicans to take a stance on the conflict. "Vote by vote, Democrats are breaking through Republicans' wall of silence on Trump's illegal war," said Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer in a statement.

cards.headline: Oil Prices Climb Following U.S.-Iran Military Exchanges
cards.teaser: Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport as the United States and Iran exchanged military strikes.
cards.body:
Oil prices climbed to their highest level in more than a week following military exchanges between Iran and the United States. Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport, hitting a passenger terminal and killing one person. The attack prompted Kuwait to briefly shut down the airport as the latest escalation in the back-and-forth strikes between the two nations.

The incident tested a fragile ceasefire and widened the conflict zone to include critical Gulf infrastructure. Energy markets reacted to the heightened risk to regional oil production and transport facilities, driving crude prices upward even as broader stock indexes declined.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Targets 59 Countries with New Forced Labor Tariffs
cards.teaser: The administration plans to impose tariffs of up to 12.5 percent on countries that fail to address goods made with forced labor.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced tariffs of up to 12.5 percent on 59 countries and the European Union, citing concerns about forced labor in imported goods. The administration framed this approach as a legal and political shift following the US Supreme Court's rejection of many of the president's previous tariff measures in February.

Critics argue the forced labor rationale serves as cover for broader protectionist trade goals. The new justification represents how the administration is recalibrating its defense of tariff policies after facing legal setbacks.

cards.headline: Trump signs order moving thousands of federal workers into at-will employment
cards.teaser: President Trump signed an executive order creating a new employment classification that makes it easier to fire about 8,000 federal workers in policy roles.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order on Wednesday that strips job protections from approximately 8,000 senior federal workers earning up to nearly $200,000 annually. The order creates a new employment classification for workers deemed to be "influencing" government policy, moving them into at-will positions where they can be dismissed more easily.

The move eliminates civil service protections that typically insulate career federal employees from removal. This represents a renewed push by the Trump administration to restructure the federal workforce, following a similar attempt during his first term known as Schedule F.

cards.headline: Iranian attack on Kuwait airport kills one, injures dozens as ceasefire falters
cards.teaser: Iran launched missiles and drones at targets in Kuwait and Bahrain, killing at least one person and injuring dozens at Kuwait's airport.
cards.body:
Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main airport, killing one person and injuring dozens others. The attack forced Kuwait to briefly shut the airport's passenger terminal. Iran said the strike was retaliation for earlier US military action against an Iranian oil tanker and island.

The incident represents another test of the fragile ceasefire between the United States and Iran. The back-and-forth attacks between the two countries continue to destabilize the agreement and threaten regional security.

cards.headline: Trump intervenes in Brazilian politics ahead of election
cards.teaser: The president appears ready to support a right-wing ally before a crucial vote testing Latin America's left.
cards.body:
President Trump has inserted himself into Brazilian politics ahead of a major election this year. Trump appears prepared to support a new right-wing ally in the upcoming vote, which will serve as a significant test for leftist movements across Latin America.

The election represents the biggest challenge for the Latin American left in the current political cycle. Trump's involvement marks another instance of the president attempting to influence electoral outcomes in the region, having previously agitated Brazilian politics during his time in office.

cards.headline: Countries accelerate island building in South China Sea
cards.teaser: After years of watching China create land to back its claims, other nations are doing the same.
cards.body:
Countries in the South China Sea region have begun their own land creation projects after years of observing China's island building activities. The shift represents a new phase in territorial disputes over the contested waters.

China has spent years constructing artificial islands to support its expansive territorial claims in the South China Sea. Other nations with competing claims now appear to have adopted a strategy of matching China's approach by creating their own land features to strengthen their positions.

cards.headline: Israeli strikes kill nine in Lebanon as Hezbollah fires rockets
cards.teaser: The attacks strain a partial ceasefire agreed by Israel and the Lebanese armed group.
cards.body:
Israeli forces conducted strikes in southern Lebanon, killing nine people, while Hezbollah fired rockets across the border. The violence tested a partial ceasefire agreement reached between Israel and the Lebanese armed group on Monday.

Despite the truce, Israel's military operations continued in the south, though strikes have not targeted Beirut following the US-brokered deal. Both sides engaged in a second day of ceasefire negotiations as the fragile agreement remained under strain.

cards.headline: Fire at New Delhi hotel kills at least 21
cards.teaser: Dozens more were injured in what appears to be the deadliest fire in the Indian capital in at least four years.
cards.body:
A fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more. The blaze ranks as the deadliest fire in India's capital in at least four years.

Authorities responded to the hotel fire, which caused significant casualties among guests and staff. The incident adds to a history of deadly fires in Indian buildings, where safety standards and enforcement have long been concerns.

cards.headline: Trump to impose tariffs on dozens of nations over forced labor claims
cards.teaser: The administration plans tariffs on approximately 60 trading partners including China, the UK, and EU countries.
cards.body:
President Trump has announced tariffs of 10-12.5% on approximately 60 trading partners, including the UK, Canada, the EU, Taiwan, and Australia. The administration is citing alleged forced labor violations as the justification for these trade penalties.

The move follows the US Supreme Court's rejection of many of Trump's previous tariffs in February. The EU has already responded critically, stating that the new duties breach the spirit of a tariff agreement reached with the US last July.

cards.headline: Portugal and Austria win UN Security Council seats over Germany
cards.teaser: Germany suffered a major diplomatic setback in the vote for two available council seats.
cards.body:
Portugal and Austria have won two of the available seats on the UN Security Council, defeating Germany in the voting process. The result represents a significant diplomatic setback for Germany, which had actively campaigned for one of the positions.

The election marked an unusual defeat for a major European power in UN elections. Five countries in total were elected to the Security Council in the voting process.

cards.headline: Trump removes job protections from 8,000 federal workers
cards.teaser: An executive order moves thousands of federal positions to a new employment category that makes them easier to fire.
cards.body:
President Trump signed an executive order removing job protections from approximately 8,000 federal workers earning up to about $200,000 annually. These employees, deemed to be "influencing" government policy, can now be fired without the usual civil service protections.

The move strips job security from a mostly senior group of federal workers across various agencies. It represents an expansion of presidential control over the federal workforce and part of the administration's broader effort to overhaul how the government operates.

cards.headline: Trump-backed candidate loses Iowa governor primary
cards.teaser: A farmer supported by the MAHA movement defeated the president's endorsed candidate in the Republican primary.
cards.body:
A MAHA-aligned candidate defeated the Trump-endorsed choice in Iowa's Republican primary for governor. The loss represents a notable setback for Trump's endorsement power in a GOP primary contest.

The result underscores potential limits to Trump's influence within the Republican Party when facing candidates backed by competing movements. Iowa's primary outcome has drawn national attention as the state plays a significant role in early presidential politics.

cards.headline: Senate advances ICE funding package along party lines
cards.teaser: The Senate voted to begin debate on a Republican bill funding immigration enforcement through the end of Trump's term.
cards.body:
The Senate voted along party lines to advance a Republican bill that would fund Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations through the end of President Trump's term. The procedural vote allows debate and amendments to proceed on the legislation.

Democrats opposed the measure, highlighting the partisan divide over immigration enforcement funding and policy priorities.

cards.headline: Three Royal Navy personnel die in helicopter crash
cards.teaser: A Royal Navy helicopter crashed during a training exercise in Devon.
cards.body:
Three members of the Royal Navy died when their helicopter crashed during a training exercise in Devon, England. The Royal Family, the prime minister, and the head of the navy offered condolences following the incident.

The crash occurred during routine training operations. Military aviation accidents during peacetime training exercises remain relatively rare but highlight the inherent risks of military service even outside combat zones.

cards.headline: Israeli strikes kill nine in Lebanon as ceasefire strains
cards.teaser: The attacks and Hezbollah rocket fire came just days after Israel and the Lebanese group agreed to a partial ceasefire.
cards.body:
Israeli military strikes killed nine people in Lebanon as Hezbollah fired rockets across the border, threatening a partial ceasefire reached just two days earlier. Both sides have accused each other of violating the agreement's terms.

The renewed violence is part of a broader pattern of escalating tensions across the region. Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main airport, forcing a brief closure of the passenger terminal, as Iran retaliated against earlier U.S. strikes on an Iranian oil tanker and island. These incidents underscore the fragility of multiple ceasefires in the Middle East.

hero.headline: SpaceX Sets $135 Share Price for Record-Breaking IPO
hero.body:
SpaceX has set a share price of $135 for its initial public offering, positioning the company for what would be the largest IPO in history. The pricing values Elon Musk's rocket manufacturer at $1.75 trillion and is expected to exceed the record set by Saudi Aramco's 2019 public debut in both total valuation and capital raised.

The company set its target price for buyers earlier than market observers anticipated. The $135 per share pricing represents the baseline for what is expected to be a $75 billion capital raise, according to some projections. The valuation marks a significant milestone for the private space exploration company as it transitions to public ownership.

However, the path to the IPO has shown signs of uncertainty. The company has lowered its target valuation multiple times in recent weeks, raising questions about market conditions and investor appetite for the offering. Market analysts have pointed to these repeated downward adjustments as a potential warning signal for broader stock market sentiment.

SpaceX has cited substantial capital needs as a driver for the public offering. The company's operations span rocket manufacturing, satellite deployment, and space exploration initiatives, all of which require ongoing investment. The decision to go public comes as the company scales its Starship program and expands its Starlink satellite internet service.

The IPO is scheduled to proceed in the coming weeks, pending final regulatory approval. If completed at the announced price, the offering would dwarf previous records and test investor demand for high-valuation technology companies. The Saudi Aramco offering raised approximately $29.4 billion in 2019, making it the previous record holder for largest IPO by capital raised.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall, Ending S&P 500's Nine-Session Winning Streak
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 620 points as technology stocks weakened and oil prices climbed.
cards.body:
Major U.S. stock indexes declined today, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropping 620 points. The pullback ended the S&P 500's nine-session winning streak, while the Nasdaq also fell as technology stocks faced selling pressure.

Oil prices climbed to their highest level in more than a week, adding to market turbulence. Bond yields rose alongside equities, while weakness in the technology sector contributed to broader index losses after an extended rally.

cards.headline: Alphabet Raises $85 Billion for Google's AI Operations
cards.teaser: The record-breaking stock sale for Google's artificial intelligence business represents the largest capital raise of its kind.
cards.body:
Alphabet completed a record-breaking $85 billion stock sale dedicated to Google's artificial intelligence operations. Goldman Sachs noted the transaction represents unprecedented territory for Wall Street.

Market analysts interpret the successful offering as a strong indicator of investor confidence in the technology sector, particularly for artificial intelligence infrastructure and development initiatives.

cards.headline: Seven States Sue Trump Administration Over Offshore Wind Deal
cards.teaser: The lawsuit challenges a nearly $1 billion payment to halt a wind farm project off the Atlantic coast.
cards.body:
Seven states, including New York, filed a lawsuit challenging a Trump administration deal that paid a French company approximately $1 billion to cancel offshore wind farm projects. The states argue the administration exceeded its authority by using federal funds to block renewable energy development.

The legal challenge contends the payment undermines the states' climate and energy goals. The lawsuit raises questions about whether the administration had the power to allocate federal resources in this manner.

cards.headline: Broadcom Stock Falls Despite Earnings Beat and Raised Forecast
cards.teaser: Shares declined after the company reported results that showed growth in AI chip sales but weaker software revenue.
cards.body:
Broadcom shares declined despite beating earnings expectations and raising forward guidance. The chipmaker's artificial intelligence chip segment demonstrated strong growth, but investors reacted negatively to weaker software revenue results.

The stock slide occurred as the broader tech sector faced headwinds, with the Nasdaq dropping and the S&P 500 snapping a nine-day winning streak. The market's focus on Broadcom's underperforming software division overshadowed gains in its semiconductor business.

hero.headline: NASA declares Mars orbiter MAVEN dead after months of silence
hero.body:
NASA has officially ended operations for its Mars Atmosphere and Volatile Evolution spacecraft, known as MAVEN, after the orbiter stopped communicating with ground stations more than a decade into its mission.

The spacecraft abruptly ceased transmitting data over the weekend. NASA reported that all systems were functioning normally before MAVEN passed behind Mars. When the orbiter emerged from behind the planet, ground controllers received only silence. "Telemetry showed all subsystems working normally before it orbited behind Mars," the agency stated. "The spacecraft and operations teams are investigating the anomaly to address the situation."

Launched in 2013, MAVEN arrived at Mars the following year with a primary mission lasting just one year. The spacecraft far exceeded expectations, operating successfully for more than a decade while studying the upper Martian atmosphere and its interaction with the solar wind. The data collected by MAVEN helped scientists understand a fundamental transformation in Mars' history. Scientists determined that the sun's solar wind gradually stripped away most of the planet's atmosphere over billions of years, converting Mars from a warm, wet world into the cold, dry planet visible today.

Beyond its atmospheric research, MAVEN served as a crucial communication relay for NASA's rovers exploring the Martian surface, including Curiosity and Perseverance. These rovers have made numerous scientific discoveries that depended partly on MAVEN's relay capabilities.

The loss of MAVEN reduces NASA's active spacecraft presence at Mars. Two other orbiters remain operational around the red planet: the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, launched in 2005, and Mars Odyssey, launched in 2001. However, neither of these spacecraft can fully replicate MAVEN's specialized atmospheric measurements, creating a gap in the types of scientific observations that were previously available.

The emotional impact of MAVEN's loss has resonated across the NASA team. Many scientists and engineers spent more than a decade working directly with the orbiter, forming strong professional connections to the mission. The spacecraft produced hundreds of peer-reviewed scientific papers that fundamentally reshaped our understanding of Martian climate history.

NASA has not announced immediate plans to replace MAVEN's atmospheric monitoring capabilities. The agency continues developing future Mars missions, including an ambitious sample return campaign that would bring rocks collected by Perseverance back to Earth for detailed laboratory analysis. Future Mars orbiters may incorporate atmospheric instruments similar to those carried by MAVEN, but no timeline has been established for such missions. For now, NASA faces a significant gap in its ability to monitor Mars' upper atmosphere and track how the planet continues to lose gases to space.

cards.headline: Flesh-eating screwworm detected in South Texas
cards.teaser: The USDA reported a potential screwworm infection in South Texas, which would mark the first time the parasite has crossed the US-Mexico border.
cards.body:
The United States Department of Agriculture announced the detection of a flesh-eating screwworm infection in South Texas. The finding represents a potential breach of the US-Mexico border by the parasite, which has not been detected in the United States in decades.

Screwworms are fly larvae that burrow into the flesh of living animals and humans, feeding on tissue. The USDA said the case is under investigation and awaiting confirmation. If verified, it would signal a significant change in the geographic range of the parasite, which has been eradicated from the United States through sustained control programs.

cards.headline: Alphabet raises record $85 billion for Google AI operations
cards.teaser: Alphabet completed an $85 billion stock sale to fund Google's artificial intelligence business, marking the largest such raise on record.
cards.body:
Alphabet is conducting the largest equity fundraising ever, selling up to $85 billion in stock to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure investments. The sale includes a $10 billion share purchase from Berkshire Hathaway, the investment firm previously led by Warren Buffett.

The massive capital raise exceeds the combined value of the three largest IPOs on record, underscoring investor confidence in AI development. The funds will support Google's expansion of AI capabilities as the company competes with other major technology firms investing heavily in artificial intelligence systems.

cards.headline: Google ordered to add clearer links in AI search results
cards.teaser: Google must modify its AI Overviews feature to include clearer source links and allow UK publishers to opt out of having their content used.
cards.body:
Regulators in the UK have ordered Google to make changes to its AI Overviews feature following complaints from publishers. The Competition and Markets Authority ruled that Google must provide clearer links to original sources and allow publishers to opt out of having their content included in AI-generated search summaries.

The decision gives news organisations and online publishers greater control over their content and strengthens their position in negotiating deals with Google. Publishers had raised concerns about declining click-through traffic and revenue as users relied on AI summaries instead of visiting original sources.

cards.headline: Dashlane says 20 encrypted password vaults were stolen
cards.teaser: Password manager Dashlane issued a security advisory stating that 20 encrypted vaults were taken, but provided few details about the incident.
cards.body:
Dashlane reported that 20 encrypted password vaults were stolen in a security incident. The password management company issued an advisory warning affected users but omitted key details about how the breach occurred or when it was discovered.

The company has not provided additional information about the incident or responded to questions. Encrypted vaults contain user passwords and other sensitive information protected by encryption, which requires the user's master password to decrypt. Dashlane did not specify whether the affected accounts had additional security measures like two-factor authentication enabled.

cards.headline: Google releases Gemma 4 12B model for laptops with 16GB RAM
cards.teaser: Google introduced Gemma 4 12B, an artificial intelligence model designed to run locally on laptops with 16 gigabytes of memory.
cards.body:
Google released Gemma 4 12B, a multimodal AI model built to operate on laptops with 16 gigabytes of RAM. The model uses a new encoding approach and token prediction method to deliver performance beyond what its size would typically suggest.

Gemma 4 12B represents an encoder-free design that can process audio and video in addition to text. The model runs entirely on local hardware without requiring cloud connectivity. Google designed the system to enable AI workflows that operate independently of remote servers, giving users more control over their data and reducing latency in AI operations.

cards.headline: Lovable expands Google Cloud partnership fivefold
cards.teaser: Lovable signed a multi-year agreement with Google Cloud to increase its usage by five times, including expanded access to Anthropic Claude.
cards.body:
Lovable and Google Cloud signed an expanded multi-year contract that increases Lovable's cloud infrastructure footprint by five times. The agreement also provides Lovable with broader access to Anthropic's Claude AI system.

The deal reflects growing demand for cloud computing resources as companies scale their operations and adopt artificial intelligence tools. Lovable's expansion on Google Cloud infrastructure represents a significant increase in its technical capacity. The partnership includes access to Anthropic's Claude models, which run on cloud platforms through partnership agreements.

hero.headline: Liverpool defender Konate says depression followed deaths of Jota and father
hero.body:
Liverpool defender Ibrahima Konate has disclosed that he struggled with depression during his final season at the club following the deaths of teammate Diogo Jota and his father. The French international opened up about the mental health challenges he faced while dealing with the twin losses.

Konate's revelation highlights the personal toll professional athletes can face beyond their on-field performances. The defender continued to play for Liverpool while coping with grief, a period he described as marked by significant mental health struggles. His decision to speak publicly about depression adds to growing conversations within professional sports about mental health awareness.

The deaths of Jota, a fellow Liverpool player, and Konate's father occurred during what would become the defender's last season with the club. The timing compounded the emotional difficulty for Konate, who was simultaneously managing his professional responsibilities while processing profound personal loss. Depression among athletes has gained increased attention in recent years as more players have shared their experiences with mental health challenges.

Konate's openness about his battle with depression follows a trend of athletes discussing mental health more candidly. The pressures of elite competition, combined with personal tragedy, created circumstances that affected his wellbeing during a period when he remained in the public eye as a professional footballer. His willingness to discuss these struggles publicly may help reduce stigma around mental health issues in sports.

The defender's disclosure comes after his departure from Liverpool, allowing him perspective on a difficult chapter in his career and personal life. By sharing his experience with depression, Konate joins other prominent athletes who have spoken about mental health, contributing to broader efforts to normalize discussions about psychological wellbeing in professional sports.

cards.headline: NBA Finals begin with Knicks visiting Spurs
cards.teaser: The 2026 NBA Finals tip off with the New York Knicks facing the San Antonio Spurs in Game 1.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks face the San Antonio Spurs in the 2026 NBA Finals, with Game 1 airing on ABC. The matchup represents a significant moment for the Knicks, whose last championship came in 1973.

The Spurs counter with Victor Wembanyama, the NBA's brightest young star, competing on the sport's biggest stage. The Finals showcase one of basketball's most storied franchises in New York returning to championship relevance.

cards.headline: Bucks explore trade market for Antetokounmpo as Heat wait
cards.teaser: The Milwaukee Bucks are surveying the trade market for Giannis Antetokounmpo while the Miami Heat await developments.
cards.body:
Milwaukee is scanning the market for potential trades involving star forward Giannis Antetokounmpo. The Miami Heat are waiting for a final decision as the Bucks evaluate their options with the two-time MVP.

Trade speculation has included the Heat and Boston Celtics as potential destinations for Antetokounmpo. A move to Portland is considered unlikely according to reports. The trade discussions are unfolding as the NBA Finals get underway.

cards.headline: Arrest warrant issued for 49ers receiver Brandon Aiyuk
cards.teaser: San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk is wanted on a warrant connected to a misdemeanor speeding charge.
cards.body:
An arrest warrant has been issued for 49ers star Brandon Aiyuk in connection with a misdemeanor speeding charge. The warrant follows a viral video showing speeding near Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara.

Aiyuk appeared to respond to news of the warrant with a racing photograph on social media. The legal issue adds uncertainty to Aiyuk's future with the 49ers, which was already unclear heading into the offseason.

cards.headline: Packers linebacker Parsons out until at least October
cards.teaser: Green Bay Packers linebacker Micah Parsons will miss the start of the season after undergoing a meniscus procedure.
cards.body:
Micah Parsons will not return to the field until at least mid-October following surgery on his meniscus. The Packers linebacker revealed he had the procedure and discussed his rehabilitation timeline.

Parsons will miss the opening weeks of the season as he recovers. His potential return in Week 6 could come in a primetime matchup against the Dallas Cowboys, his former team before joining Green Bay.

cards.headline: Former Alabama coach Nick Saban backs college sports bill
cards.teaser: Nick Saban testified before Congress in support of legislation to regulate college athletics as major conferences push back.
cards.body:
Nick Saban testified before Congress in support of bipartisan legislation designed to reform college athletics governance. The former Alabama coach emphasized the need for regulatory structure to bring order to a sport that has undergone significant changes in recent years.

The proposed bill addresses key issues affecting college sports, including compensation rules for athlete names, images and likenesses. Despite Saban's backing, the legislation faces opposition from major conferences, including the SEC and Big Ten, signaling a divide over how college athletics should be regulated moving forward.

cards.headline: Sabalenka loses at French Open as Grand Slam chance slips away
cards.teaser: Top-ranked Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock loss at the French Open, missing another opportunity to win a major title.
cards.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shocking defeat at the French Open, losing to Diana Shnaider 3-6 7-5 6-0. Sabalenka's title bid unraveled in the third set, where she experienced a complete collapse against her opponent.

The loss represents another missed opportunity for the top-ranked player at a Grand Slam tournament. Sabalenka has now failed to capture the French Open title despite entering as the championship favorite.

hero.headline: CBS News fires 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley after clash with producer
hero.body:
CBS News has fired veteran correspondent Scott Pelley from 60 Minutes following a heated confrontation with the network's new leadership. The termination was announced after Pelley clashed with executives during a staff meeting this week.

The firing came in the wake of broader cuts at 60 Minutes announced the previous Thursday, when CBS News management removed the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents, Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi, without providing specific reasons for their departures.

During a Monday morning staff meeting with newly appointed executive editor Nick Bilton and CBS News managing editor Charles Forelle, Pelley directly attacked Bari Weiss, the network's editor-in-chief who joined in October. According to the Guardian, Pelley told executives that Weiss was "murdering 60 Minutes" and accused her of being "brought in to kill it."

In a message sent Tuesday evening, Bilton informed Pelley that he had been "terminated for cause effective immediately." Bilton referenced Pelley's conduct during the meeting, writing: "Yesterday, you hijacked my first meeting with staff to disparage me, my qualifications, and my intentions with remarkable incivility and contempt."

Weiss stated that Pelley had violated "trust and mutual respect," though she provided no additional details about the specific nature of the conflict.

Pelley has since issued a public statement accusing CBS News executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He also claimed executives pushed unverified claims and gave politicians a say in editorial decisions.

The departures represent significant changes for 60 Minutes, which has long been considered one of television's most prominent investigative journalism programs. The show now has only three full-time correspondents as it approaches its 59th season this fall: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker, and L Jon Wertheim, with Norah O'Donnell contributing from across the network. Anderson Cooper announced earlier this year that he would be leaving the show.

Former 60 Minutes correspondent Steve Kroft called the situation under Weiss's leadership "disastrous," describing it as "journalistic interference" that makes "no business sense whatsoever," despite the show remaining the highest-rated program in its category.

Rachel Maddow characterized the changes as an "oligarchic takeover" of CBS News, while longtime producer Rome Hartman praised Pelley as "among the all-time greats of CBS News and of 60 Minutes."

The firing has sparked debate within the journalism community about editorial independence and the future direction of 60 Minutes, which has maintained its reputation as a flagship news program for decades despite the recent internal turmoil.

cards.headline: Wim Wenders withdraws 1975 film over scene with underage actress
cards.teaser: The director pulled Wrong Move from circulation because of a topless scene featuring Nastassja Kinski, who was 13 during filming.
cards.body:
German director Wim Wenders has withdrawn his 1975 film Wrong Move from circulation due to a topless scene featuring actress Nastassja Kinski, who was 13 years old during filming. In a statement released Wednesday, Wenders instructed streaming services, television broadcasters and distribution partners to make the film no longer publicly accessible.

Wenders acknowledged that the child actor should have been better protected during production. The decision reflects a reassessment of content that does not align with current standards for safeguarding minor performers on set.

cards.headline: Tom Holland addresses earlier comments about playing Spider-Man past 30
cards.teaser: The actor, now 30, said his 2021 statement about playing Spider-Man in his thirties may have been a negotiating strategy.
cards.body:
In 2021, Tom Holland told GQ magazine that continuing to play Spider-Man beyond age 30 would indicate he had made a mistake. Now 30 himself, Holland has reconsidered that statement, suggesting it may have been a negotiating tactic. He explained to an interviewer that he could have been attempting to leverage Sony into offering him a better deal—a strategy designed to create pressure in contract discussions.

Holland's latest Spider-Man film, Brand New Day, releases July 31. He currently has no plans to exit the role, offering a glimpse into how actors use public statements strategically during negotiations with major studios.

cards.headline: NBA Finals begin with Knicks facing Spurs
cards.teaser: The championship series between New York and San Antonio tips off, with games available to stream online.
cards.body:
The NBA Finals 2026 pit the New York Knicks against the San Antonio Spurs in a championship matchup that marks a significant moment for both franchises. The Knicks are working to end their long championship drought, with their last title coming in 1973. The Spurs counter with Victor Wembanyama, the brightest young star in the NBA, competing on the sport's biggest stage.

The series will play out over the coming weeks as both teams battle for the Larry O'Brien Championship Trophy. Fans can watch the games through multiple streaming options, including some free viewing methods available online.

cards.headline: Lauv withdraws from tour with Khalid citing mental health
cards.teaser: The singer announced he is dropping out of the joint tour, saying he is deeply struggling.
cards.body:
Singer Lauv announced he is withdrawing from a tour with Khalid, citing mental health struggles. In a statement posted Tuesday, Lauv wrote that he has to be honest with himself and his audience, saying he is deeply struggling right now.

The singer said he was trying to be strong but made the decision to step away from the scheduled performances. Lauv did not provide a timeline for his return to touring or specify what mental health challenges he is facing. The announcement leaves Khalid to continue the tour without his planned co-headliner.

cards.headline: ElevenLabs licenses Hasbro characters for AI applications
cards.teaser: The AI audio company partnered with Hasbro to use characters including Transformers and Mr. Potato Head.
cards.body:
AI audio startup ElevenLabs partnered with Hasbro to license a collection of the toy company's characters for use in artificial intelligence applications. The partnership brings characters including Optimus Prime from Transformers, Mr. Potato Head, and figures from Monopoly and Clue to ElevenLabs' Iconic Marketplace.

The deal was announced through a collaboration with Hasbro's AI Studios division. The licensing agreement allows ElevenLabs to use the characters' likenesses and identities in its AI audio products. The partnership represents an expansion of how traditional entertainment properties are being adapted for emerging AI technologies.

cards.headline: TikTok and Sundance Institute launch microseries writing program
cards.teaser: The four-week online course aims to support creators developing short-form scripted content for digital platforms.
cards.body:
TikTok and Sundance Institute are launching a microseries writing program through Sundance Collab, the institute's digital learning and community platform. The initiative aims to support creators writing and producing microdramas and other short-form scripted series for digital audiences.

The four-week live online course will run later this year. The program represents an effort to develop the next generation of creator-led short-form storytelling specifically designed for digital viewing. Sundance Collab provides online educational resources for filmmakers and content creators.

hero.headline: Trump signs order moving thousands of federal workers into at-will employment
hero.teaser: President Trump signed an executive order creating a new employment classification that makes it easier to fire about 8,000 federal workers in policy roles.
hero.body:
President Trump signed an executive order on Wednesday that strips job protections from approximately 8,000 senior federal workers earning up to nearly $200,000 annually. The order creates a new employment classification for workers deemed to be "influencing" government policy, moving them into at-will positions where they can be dismissed more easily.

The move eliminates civil service protections that typically insulate career federal employees from removal. This represents a renewed push by the Trump administration to restructure the federal workforce, following a similar attempt during his first term known as Schedule F.

cards.headline: Trump to announce $700 million in coal industry funding
cards.teaser: President Trump plans to use wartime authority to direct $700 million to existing coal plants and export infrastructure.
cards.body:
President Trump is expected to announce that his administration will provide approximately $700 million to support the coal industry. The president plans to invoke wartime authority under the Defense Prevention Act to allocate the funding.

The package includes $425 million for 13 existing coal plants, $75 million for an export terminal in California, and $185 million for additional coal-related projects. The use of the Defense Prevention Act allows the administration to direct industrial production and funding based on national security justifications.

cards.headline: Stars and Stripes board members sue Pentagon over editorial restrictions
cards.teaser: Two advisory board members filed a lawsuit alleging the Defense Department is attempting to exert unprecedented control over the military newspaper.
cards.body:
Two advisory board members for the Stars and Stripes military newspaper filed a lawsuit against the Pentagon on Wednesday. The suit alleges that the Defense Department's overhaul of the publication undermines its editorial independence.

The lawsuit asks a federal judge to block what the plaintiffs describe as the Pentagon's efforts to exert unprecedented control over the news outlet. Stars and Stripes has historically operated with editorial independence despite being affiliated with the military. The board members argue that recent departmental changes threaten that tradition.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins New Mexico Democratic gubernatorial primary
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official secured the Democratic nomination and could become the first female Native American governor if elected.
cards.body:
Deb Haaland, who served in President Biden's administration, won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico on Wednesday. The victory positions her to compete in the general election for the state's top executive office.

If Haaland wins in November, she would make history as the first female Native American governor in the United States. Her primary victory marks a significant step in her campaign to lead New Mexico.

cards.headline: California governor primary results show Hilton and Becerra leading
cards.teaser: Early results in California's gubernatorial primary show Steve Hilton and Xavier Becerra ahead as votes continue to be counted.
cards.body:
With nearly 60% of votes counted in California's gubernatorial primary, Republican Steve Hilton held a narrow lead over Democrat Xavier Becerra. Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News host, and Becerra, the former health secretary, are positioned as their parties' likely nominees to replace Governor Gavin Newsom.

Progressive billionaire Tom Steyer trailed in third place among the leading candidates. President Trump congratulated Hilton on Wednesday for his leading position, though vote counting was still underway and the race had not been officially called.

cards.headline: Trump says UFC arena on White House grounds may become permanent
cards.teaser: President Trump suggested the UFC arena under construction on the South Lawn might remain as a permanent installation.
cards.body:
President Trump has suggested the UFC arena being constructed on the White House South Lawn could become permanent. In a video posted to his TikTok account, Trump compared the structure to the Eiffel Tower while discussing the possibility of keeping it indefinitely.

The arena is being built for a series of UFC fights scheduled for June 14, known as the Freedom 250 fight card. Trump directed the installation of the temporary venue on the South Lawn, though he has now indicated it may never be removed.

cards.headline: Trump attacks CNN journalist during Oval Office remarks
cards.teaser: President Trump accused CNN's Kaitlan Collins of having hatred in her eyes while taking questions from reporters.
cards.body:
President Trump criticized CNN journalist Kaitlan Collins on Wednesday while responding to reporter questions in the Oval Office. Trump accused Collins of having hatred in her eyes and referred to CNN as "crooked as hell."

The exchange occurred as Trump was discussing the recently defunct anti-weaponization fund, which he characterized positively. He then directed his criticism toward CNN and Collins specifically during the press interaction.
